- MEDIUM `[loop-owned-invariants]`: The Architecture section and the plan-body Acceptance criteria attribute **429 detection** and **`wait_until_epoch` honoring** to the shared leaf — "The shared loop owns only what is identical across both: **429 detection**, the wait-vs-switch policy … and **`wait_until_epoch` honoring**" and "covers … all four loop-owned invariants: **429 detection** … and **`wait_until_epoch` honoring**" — but step 1 (`01-plan-tool-rate-limit-loop-py-shared.md`, Implementation) deliberately makes both caller-injected seams the leaf never performs: classification "yields a small loop-legible result … The loop never inspects `failure` — doing so would need `ClaudeFailureKind`, a first-party type", and the wait is "**`wait(target_epoch) -> bool`** — wraps `wait_until_epoch` … Wrapping to a bool keeps `WaitUntilAction` out of the leaf." The detail is authoritative (stdlib-only forces detection and epoch-honoring out of the leaf) and its own acceptance bullet already rewords these to "rate-limit wait-or-switch handling … honoring the injected wait's RETRY/STOP result"; the body lags and instructs testing "429 detection" in `tests/test_rate_limit_loop.py`, where the fake injects categories and detection cannot be exercised.
- MEDIUM `[ask-switch-selection]`: Step 1 (`01-plan-tool-rate-limit-loop-py-shared.md`, Implementation) describes the `select_backend` seam as "Used by the SWITCH auto-swap **and the ASK-switch**," but in the live code the ASK-switch's `_select_rate_limit_backend` call happens **inside** `_ask_rate_limit_action` (shell.py:311-317 returns `OnRateLimitAction.SWITCH` only after the swap already succeeded), so the leaf itself invokes `select_backend` only on the auto-SWITCH policy path — on an ASK-SWITCH it merely resets the guard and retries (the branch bullet already says "reset + retry"). The seam bullet conflates the caller's helper with the leaf's seam; an implementer could wire the leaf to re-select on ASK-SWITCH and double-switch the backend.
